overall: Atlanta is experiencing a warm, humid June afternoon with broken clouds and active convective potential. Temperatures peaked at 84.2°F around 12:10 ET and are now stalling or slightly retreating (30-min velocity at -3.6°F/hr, acceleration at -4.5°F/hr²), suggesting the early peak was likely a result of partial sun breaks. Thunderstorms are forecast to arrive after 1pm, which will likely cap further warming.
forecast_obs_notes: There is notable model spread: ECMWF is the most conservative at 83.8°F (very close to the current running max), NBM sits in the middle at 86.0°F, and HRRR is the bullish outlier at 89.1°F matching the NWS narrative of near 89°F. The current running max of 84.2°F already exceeds or is near the ECMWF forecast, suggesting ECMWF may verify low, but the aggressive HRRR/NWS scenario would require a meaningful secondary warming push that the current cloud cover and approaching convection make less likely.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max locked in at 84.2°F and temperatures currently retreating under broken clouds with storms approaching after 1pm, significant additional warming above 87°F appears unlikely. The INTRADAY model (obs-driven, most current) splits its probability mass evenly between 86-87°F and 88-89°F, while the fused META model favors the 88-89°F bucket at 27.1%, but this is before the apparent early-peak signal is fully weighted. A modest secondary recovery toward 86-87°F before convection arrives is the most plausible outcome, but breaching 89°F requires the HRRR scenario and favorable timing that current obs do not strongly support. Confidence is moderate-low given the split between obs-driven signals and model guidance.
